thread:
incident-bot: PAGE P1 - Neptune Corp (enterprise / VPC) — elevated streaming disconnects observed on dedicated pool dp-neptune-01 in eu-west-1. 09:12 UTC spike: ~9% streaming sessions closed with 502/504 during send. Paging oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: on it. seeing a spike in websocket CLOSE with code 1006 and downstream HTTP 502 from their appgw. adding logs now. @sre-jen FYI if this needs handoff.

sre-jen: pinged. if it's their gateway killing connections we'll want a temporary routing fallback + to ask customer to check their LB health checks. can you paste latest gateway logs?

oncall-alex: pasting snippets from dp-neptune-01 edge (trimmed):

```
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z edge[conn=812]: client=10.4.5.12 session=abc123 stream_send err=write: broken pipe
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z proxy: upstream_request id=xyz status=502 body="gateway read timeout"
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z edge[conn=813]: ws_close 1006 remote=neptune-appgw-01
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z proxy: retrying request to upstream (attempt=2) rate=high
```

oncall-alex: traffic pattern looks steady, but retries from our client side increase concurrency and blow through our backlog. suspect their gateway is intermittently returning 502 and clients are retrying without jitter.

eng-runtime-ryan: can we confirm whether prefix KV caching or batching is getting impacted? retries could cause duplicate in-flight tokens.

oncall-alex: initial check — KV cache hit rate unchanged. CPU on dp-neptune-01 nodes bumped ~15% at spike. queue length grew from 80 -> 320.

customer-success-maya: I’m on a call with Neptune SRE. They report a recent config change to their appgw (idle_timeout lowered to 30s) deployed ~09:00 UTC. Their health check logs show transient 502s around 09:10-09:13. They’re standing by to coordinate.

sre-jen: recommendation (short term): 1) Add routing rule to divert traffic for Neptune to fallback pool (dp-fallback-01) that uses model-compat variant with more permissive timeouts. 2) Apply server-side client throttling on dp-neptune-01 to prevent retry amplification. 3) Ask Neptune to temporarily increase idle_timeout and pause aggressive retry policy.

ops-luis: I can flip the routing rule. executing patch now.

ops-luis: `curl -X PATCH https://console.internal/api/routes/neptune -d '{"pool":"dp-fallback-01","override_timeouts":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'`  — applying.

incident-bot: Deploy job 98342 started (route-change) — logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/98342

eng-runtime-ryan: also enabling adaptive backpressure on dp-neptune-01 to shed inflight when queue > 200. command:

```
rbctl scale --pool dp-neptune-01 --backpressure 200
```

oncall-alex: backpressure applied. watching metrics.

(09:28 UTC) ops-luis: route-change completed, ~90% of Neptune traffic now hitting dp-fallback-01. we see errors drop on dp-neptune-01 immediately.

oncall-alex: metrics after reroute: dp-neptune-01 stream_error_rate -> 1.1% (was 9%); dp-fallback-01 error_rate ~2.7% but latency higher (tail +50ms). overall customer sessions stable. marking initial mitigation succeeded.

customer-success-maya: Neptune SRE confirms they reverted the idle_timeout change and are rolling a fix for their internal retry client (adding exponential backoff). they asked if we can keep fallback routing for 30m while they finish tests.

sre-jen: agreed. leave fallback in place for 30m. during that window we should also throttle client retries at the edge for this tenant specifically. ryan, can we add tenant-level retry limits?

eng-runtime-ryan: yes. pushing tenant guard config for tenant neptune-corp:

```
PATCH /internal/tenants/neptune-corp/guards
{ "max_concurrent_retries": 3, "min_retry_backoff_ms": 200 }
```

ryan: applied. monitoring for duplicate requests / partial outputs.

pm-nadia: tagging this incident for postmortem — impact: partial degradation for some streaming sessions, affected customers: ~2k live sessions during spike, estimated 0.6% customer-perceived errors after mitigation. will need RCA and improved integration test with customer appgw timeouts.

customer-success-maya: Neptune SRE: they’ll run a canary with updated LB config and report back in 25m. they appreciate the fast reroute.

oncall-alex: handing off monitoring to @sre-jen for the next hour. I’m heading offline for the on-call rotation.

sre-jen: taking over. I’ll keep watch, escalate to eng-runtime if error rate rises >2.5% or queue length >250.

(10:02 UTC) neptune-sre-bot: Neptune SRE status: canary passed, no 502s observed for 5m. reverting their change had immediate effect.

sre-jen: good to hear. starting rollback of route change in 5m if metrics remain stable. plan: 1) revert route to dp-neptune-01, 2) keep tenant retry guard for 1h, 3) schedule postmortem with Neptune for next business day.

ops-luis: queued route revert job 98356.

(10:17 UTC) incident-bot: Post-mitigation snapshot: final stream_error_rate (dp-neptune-01) 0.9%, dp-fallback-01 0.8% after revert. queues normalized. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-Resolved — monitor-only.

pm-nadia: added postmortem stub: /docs/incidents/3215002468-neptune-gw-integration-pm. action items: stronger tenant-level retry defaults, add e2e test simulating appgw low idle_timeout, run integration checklist with Neptune.

customer-success-maya: Neptune thanked ops and eng. They’ll coordinate config controls in their deploy pipeline to prevent lowering idle timeout without canarying.

sre-jen: closing handoff. leaving retry guard live for 1h per plan. anyone else with items?

oncall-alex: all good from my side. great cross-team response. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging. Summary: routing fallback + tenant retry guard prevented broad customer impact; root cause: customer-side appgw config change causing 502s + retry amplification. Follow-ups scheduled.
